instructed to imagine eating their favorite food or their favorite holiday while performing a reaction time task. When imagining
their favorite food, but not their favorite holiday, restrained nondieters performed as poorly as current dieters on the reaction
time task.
Although evidence seems to be mounting that the poor cognitive function of current dieters is due to psychological and not
biological factors, work still continues to examine some of the more subtle possible biological mechanisms which, may underlie
the effects. One possible mechanism is that a low dietary intake of the amino acid TRP (the precursor for 5-HT) leads dieters to
have impaired serotonergic function. However, analysis of the urine of dieters for the 5-HT metabolite, 5-hydroxyindoleacetic
